control_paper_title: Contraction extraction from term and preterm electrohysterographic signals
evidence: Vandewiele et al. screened 24 TPEHGDB ML studies and named three with a sound evaluation methodology: "we have found three machine learning studies that were accessible, tackled preterm birth risk estimation and, to the best of our knowledge, had a sound evaluation methodology [38,39,40]." Ref [40] is Sadi-Ahmed & Kadir-Talha, IEEE ICEE 2015. They later criticize this paper's accuracy metric (always-predict-term baseline) but do not place it in any of their three leakage-flaw categories (subsampled CV; same-signal train/test split; oversampling before split).

control_paper_title: Examination of single wavelet-based features of EHG signals for preterm birth classification
evidence: Same screening verdict as NC01: Vandewiele et al. list this paper as ref [39] among the three studies that "had a sound evaluation methodology [38,39,40]." They note leave-one-out scores "might be rather optimistic" but still classify the evaluation as sound and do not assign it to any of the three leakage-flaw categories.

control_paper_title: Time-frequency analysis of electrohysterogram for classification of term and preterm birth
evidence: Same screening verdict as NC01: listed as ref [38] among the three studies with "a sound evaluation methodology [38,39,40]." Stretch: they then write that Ryu et al. "evaluated the added value of their feature, by subsampling a balanced dataset of 38 term and 38 preterm records, 100 times" and that "this subsampling strategy again avoids the problem of imbalanced data" — the same class of design they elsewhere treat as a flaw. Official classification remains sound; the subsample note is why confidence is not high.

control_paper_title: HAMLET: Hierarchical Harmonic Filters for Learning Tracts from Diffusion MRI
evidence: Poulin et al. define contamination as "the usage of the same diffusion data for training and testing" and name only two methods as suffering from it (GRU [24] and MLP [23]). Of Reisert et al. [29] they write: "To validate their method, Reisert et al. [29] used a dataset of 83 human subjects from two independent cohorts. [...] The first cohort was used for training while the second one was used for testing." That is an explicit independent-split description for the leakage issue this review was checking. They do not use a blanket "clean" label, which is why confidence is medium.
